feature_results.rationale: Documented hooks run user-supplied commands at lifecycle points (sessionStart, userPromptSubmitted, preToolUse, postToolUse, agentStop, subagentStop, errorOccurred). preToolUse can approve or deny tool executions; the SDK additionally lets pre-tool hooks allow/deny/modify calls and post-tool hooks transform results.

evidence.excerpt: Hooks are a way of executing custom shell commands at strategic points in an agent's workflow, such as when an agent session starts or ends, when you enter a prompt, or when a tool is called.
This is the most powerful hook as it can **approve or deny tool executions**.
Before a tool executes | Allow / deny / modify the call

constraints.description: Available in Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app and Copilot cloud agent (cloud agent supports only a subset of events); VS Code hooks are in public preview. Events and input/output differ by surface.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review run behind a firewall that is on by default. Organization owners can customize it (allowlist, recommended allowlist toggle) from the Internet access settings tab, or disable it. Documented limitations apply.

evidence.excerpt: Learn how to control the domains and URLs that Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review can access.
By default, Copilot's access to the internet is limited by a firewall.
Organization owners can configure all firewall settings at the organization level, for both Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review.

constraints.description: Firewall only applies to processes started by the agent via its Bash tool, only within the GitHub Actions appliance, and is documented as not a comprehensive security solution. It does not apply to MCP server processes or Copilot setup steps.
Applies to Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review (GitHub-hosted), not local IDE agent mode or CLI.

feature_results.rationale: In VS Code, Copilot chat/agent sessions create a workspace snapshot before each request, and 'Restore Checkpoint' restores workspace files to that point and removes all subsequent conversation turns in one operation (with Redo). This is session-wide, not per-file. Not documented for Copilot CLI or the cloud agent in the pages checked; checkpoints do not reverse terminal commands or external effects.

evidence.excerpt: Before processing each request, VS Code creates a snapshot of affected workspace files.
VS Code removes subsequent requests from the conversation history and restores the workspace files to their state at the checkpoint.

constraints.description: Documented for Copilot chat sessions in Visual Studio Code only; no checkpoint/rewind found in Copilot CLI or cloud agent docs.
Checkpoints are temporary, do not replace Git, and do not reverse completed terminal commands, network requests or external-service changes.

queries: fetch docs.github.com CLI command reference (partial read, no checkpoint/rewind command seen)

feature_results.rationale: Enterprise audit log records Copilot plan/settings/policy/license changes and agent activity on GitHub; Copilot usage metrics APIs, dashboards and NDJSON export give admins usage visibility at enterprise, org, repo and user levels. Client prompt/session data is not in the audit log.

evidence.excerpt: Changes to your Copilot plan, such as changes to settings and policies or a user losing or receiving a license
The audit log does **not** include client session data, such as the prompts a user sends to Copilot locally.
The Copilot usage metrics APIs, which provide detailed, exportable data at the enterprise, organization, repository, and user levels.

constraints.description: Audit log and org/enterprise metrics are administrator features for Copilot Business/Enterprise organizations and enterprises.
Most usage metrics rely on client-side IDE telemetry, which end users must have enabled; Copilot Chat on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile are not included.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot code review is a dedicated PR review workflow on GitHub.com (plus IDEs and CLI) that produces review comments and applicable suggested fixes, with automatic review configuration.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot reviews your pull requests, identifies issues, and suggests fixes you can apply in a couple of clicks.
Repository owners can configure Copilot to automatically review all pull requests in the repository that are created by people with access to Copilot.

constraints.description: Org members need the Copilot code review policy enabled; Copilot Free does not include code review; unlicensed use requires Business/Enterprise with paid AI credits usage policies.
Azure DevOps support is public preview; passing suggestions to Copilot cloud agent and Copilot approvals are public preview.

queries: fetch docs.github.com Copilot code review concept page (3 pages of content)

feature_results.rationale: Official docs list 'Change code by asking Copilot to edit, refactor, or fix code' as a capability, and agent mode decides which files to change from a high-level instruction, so instruction-driven multi-location refactors are supported.

evidence.excerpt: **Change code** by asking Copilot to edit, refactor, or fix code.
In agent mode, Copilot takes a high-level task, decides which files to change, makes the edits, and runs commands as needed, iterating until the task is done.

constraints.description: Agent mode is available in Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Xcode, and Eclipse; not Neovim per the feature matrix. Agent mode may be disabled by org/enterprise admins.
Capabilities depend on plan, client, and organization policies; each agent-mode prompt consumes GitHub AI Credits.

feature_results.rationale: Official docs have a dedicated tutorial on using Copilot to generate unit and integration tests for specified code in Copilot Chat; not limited to a small set of languages per the docs.

evidence.excerpt: Use Copilot to generate unit and integration tests, and help improve code quality.

constraints.description: Tutorial prerequisites: Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, or a JetBrains IDE with the Copilot extension and a Copilot plan.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot CLI Autopilot mode (and the cloud agent) plan and execute multi-step tasks without per-step prompts, running tests and iterating until done.

evidence.excerpt: Autopilot mode lets Copilot carry a well-defined coding task through multiple steps without waiting for you after each step.
Agentic experiences can research a repository, plan changes, and complete multi-step tasks by reading files, editing code, and running tests in a cloud development environment.

constraints.description: Autopilot works best with all permissions enabled; with manual approval, tool requests needing approval are automatically denied. Available in Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app.

queries: fetch Autopilot concept and how-to pages
fetch Copilot on GitHub.com concept page

feature_results.rationale: The /delegate command (or '&' prefix) hands a task to Copilot cloud agent which works in the background and continues even if the local machine is shut down; CLI tasks/shells can also be promoted to background.

evidence.excerpt: Use /delegate when you want to hand off a task entirely and continue running even if you shut down your local machine.
Promote the running task or shell command to the background.
Copilot cloud agent can research a repository, plan changes, and implement them in the background.

constraints.description: Cloud agent usage requires a Copilot plan with cloud agent enabled (org admin policy for Business/Enterprise).

feature_results.rationale: Repositories are indexed for semantic code search used by Copilot Chat (GitHub, VS Code) and cloud agent, finding code by meaning rather than exact text.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot cloud agent uses semantic code search to find relevant code based on meaning, rather than relying solely on exact text matches with tools like `grep`.
Copilot in Visual Studio Code can use semantic indexing for workspace files from repositories hosted outside GitHub, such as GitLab and local repositories.

constraints.description: Index used by Copilot Chat in GitHub and VS Code and Copilot cloud agent; non-GitHub repo indexing is VS Code only, github.com only, policy-controlled and disabled by default.

feature_results.rationale: Users author custom agents as Markdown .agent.md profiles with YAML frontmatter, instructions, tool restrictions and (in supported environments) MCP server configuration, at repository, organization/enterprise or personal (~/.copilot/agents/) level; created via /agent in the CLI.

evidence.excerpt: An agent profile is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter. It describes the agent's purpose, gives it instructions, and can restrict its available tools. In supported environments, a profile can also configure MCP servers for that agent.
Each custom agent is defined by a Markdown file with an `.agent.md` extension.

constraints.description: Profile properties can behave differently or be ignored between environments; custom agents in JetBrains IDEs and Xcode are in public preview; MCP server config only in supported environments.

feature_results.rationale: The documented GitHub Copilot SDK (same agent runtime as Copilot CLI) lets applications register custom functions via defineTool/define_tool with description, parameter schema and handler, independent of MCP. This is an SDK surface rather than the interactive CLI/IDE products, and live tool replacement (session.setTools) is marked experimental.

evidence.excerpt: const searchIssues = defineTool("search_issues", {
Built-in, MCP, and plugin tools, and tools that other clients connected to the same session supply, are unaffected.

constraints.description: Requires building an application with the Copilot SDK (TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java, Rust); not a feature of the end-user CLI/IDE chat itself.
Replacing tools in a live session (session.tools.set) is documented as experimental.

queries: web_search for SDK custom tools (tool unavailable)

feature_results.rationale: GitHub's official Copilot FAQ names a Data Protection Agreement (DPA) that customers can enter, supporting GDPR compliance, and states Business/Enterprise data handling is governed by it.

evidence.excerpt: Yes. GitHub and customers can enter a [Data Protection Agreement](https://github.com/customer-terms/github-data-protection-agreement?locale=en-US) that supports compliance with the GDPR and similar legislation.

For the purposes outlined in our [Data Protection Agreement](https://github.com/customer-terms/github-data-protection-agreement), GitHub may store the following data for your enterprise outside your chosen region.

constraints.description: FAQ ties the DPA to Business/Enterprise subscribers' data handling; individual plans are governed by the Terms of Service and Privacy Statement with GitHub as controller.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency lets enterprises choose region (EU, Australia, US, Japan) for stored code and data, and Copilot Business/Enterprise is accessible on GHE.com. Documentation guarantees storage region only and says some data may be stored/transferred outside the region; no Copilot-specific processing (inference) region guarantee was found in fetched pages.

evidence.excerpt: When you adopt GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency, you can choose where your company's code and data are stored.
Although your code and user data are stored within your chosen region, GitHub may store certain types of data outside your region, and may need to transfer some data outside your region.
Your developers can access GitHub Copilot if you grant them access to a Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise subscription.

constraints.description: Requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (GHE.com) and Copilot Business or Enterprise; Copilot Individual is unavailable to managed users.
Available regions: EU (incl. Norway, Switzerland), Australia, US, Japan. Certain Copilot features are unavailable on GHE.com.

access_gaps: Copilot-specific model inference/processing region guarantees not verified; no web search tool available, only direct fetches.

feature_results.rationale: Individual (Free/Pro/Pro+) subscribers can opt out of model training via account settings. Business and Enterprise data is not used to train models, and documented default retention is none for IDE prompts/suggestions (28 days for other access).

evidence.excerpt: Individual subscribers can opt out of having their data used for AI model training at any time through [https://github.com/settings/copilot/features](https://github.com/settings/copilot/features?locale=en-US). Opting out does not affect your access to Copilot features.
No. GitHub does not use either Copilot Business or Enterprise data to train its models.
Access through IDE for Chat and Code Completions: Prompts and Suggestions: Not retained

constraints.description: Opt-out setting applies to Free/Pro/Pro+; Business/Enterprise are excluded from training by default rather than by a toggle. Retention is 28 days for prompts/suggestions outside IDE chat/completions (e.g. github.com, mobile, CLI) for Business/Enterprise.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot cloud agent checks newly introduced dependencies against the GitHub Advisory Database (malware advisories, High/Critical CVSS) and acts on findings. Scope is limited to dependencies the agent adds, not a general project-wide scan by the assistant; no ecosystem list found.

evidence.excerpt: Newly introduced dependencies are checked against the **GitHub Advisory Database** for malware advisories, and for any CVSS-rated High or Critical vulnerabilities.

constraints.description: Applies to Copilot cloud agent; can be disabled in agent settings; does not require GitHub Advanced Security license.

access_gaps: Did not check Dependabot/GitHub Advanced Security docs for wider project-level SCA surfaced to Copilot.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub docs say assistive suggestions are reviewed and applied by the user, and that agent-mode edits stream into the editor where the user can review and undo them. However, the VS Code docs (first-party Microsoft page for the Copilot client) state that for Copilot harness sessions edits are saved directly and not held in a pending review state, with Keep/Undo available for local-harness sessions, and that the review UI is under active development. This does not clearly meet 'diff with accept/reject before being written to disk', nor the whole-file-only partial definition, and varies by client/harness.

evidence.excerpt: Review streamed edits as they appear and undo any you do not want.
Assistive. Copilot responds while you work, suggesting code, answering questions, or explaining code. You review and apply each suggestion.

constraints.description: Review behavior differs by client (VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains) and by agent harness; not confirmed per-hunk accept/reject before write.

access_gaps: VS Code review-code-edits page is not in the known source registry and its exact <title> could not be captured, so it was not registered as a source; its statement that Copilot-harness edits are saved directly (Keep/Undo only for local-harness sessions) conflicts with a clear 'review before write' status.
No GitHub-docs page confirming per-hunk accept/reject for Copilot Edit mode, JetBrains, or Visual Studio was retrieved; Copilot changelog not searched for this.

feature_results.rationale: No explicit statement of in-transit and at-rest encryption for Copilot customer data was found in the official pages that could be fetched. The Copilot Trust Center (likely source) is a JavaScript-rendered page whose content could not be read; several guessed docs URLs returned 404.

access_gaps: Trust Center page content not rendered by fetch tool (JS app).
No web_search tool available in this session to locate the relevant docs page.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot Business/Enterprise are managed by GitHub org/enterprise administrators who set policies and grant seats; GitHub Enterprise Cloud supports SAML or OIDC authentication with SCIM provisioning. Dedicated Copilot-specific role names were not enumerated in fetched pages.

evidence.excerpt: Includes management of authentication and user lifecycles from an external identity management system: **SCIM** for provisioning **SAML** or **OIDC** for authentication
Access to Copilot Business and Enterprise is managed by your GitHub Administrator.
Made for organizations and enterprises, this plan offers centralized management and Copilot policy control for organization members.

constraints.description: SSO comes via GitHub Enterprise Cloud; Copilot Business/Enterprise provide admin-managed access and policy control. Copilot is not available for GitHub Enterprise Server.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot CLI has a documented offline mode (COPILOT_OFFLINE=true) that stops it contacting GitHub servers when paired with a local/on-prem BYOK model provider. This covers the CLI only; the IDE, web, mobile and cloud surfaces require connectivity, and the default Copilot-hosted models need the network. Docs do not state that the whole product works with zero network access.

evidence.excerpt: You can run Copilot CLI in offline mode to prevent it from contacting GitHub's servers. This is designed for isolated environments where the CLI should communicate only with your local or on-premises model provider.
Offline mode only guarantees full network isolation if your provider is also local or within the same isolated environment.

constraints.description: Offline mode is documented only for Copilot CLI, not for IDE extensions or other surfaces.
Requires a local or on-premises BYOK model provider (e.g. Ollama, vLLM, Foundry Local) that supports tool calling and streaming.

queries: fetch: docs.github.com BYOK models Copilot CLI (Running in offline mode section)

feature_results.rationale: Copilot CLI documents performing git operations: committing changes, reverting commits, and working on an issue in a suitably named branch, plus branching and pushing as part of PR workflows.

evidence.excerpt: Use Copilot to help you perform Git operations. `Commit the changes to this repo` `Revert the last commit, leaving the changes unstaged`
I've been assigned this issue: https://github.com/octo-org/octo-repo/issues/1234. Start working on this for me in a suitably named branch.
Getting help with commit messages and summaries.

constraints.description: Documented for Copilot CLI (commits/branches); commit-message help is documented for GitHub Desktop.

queries: fetch: Where to use GitHub Copilot
access_gaps: IDE commit-message generation doc page URL returned 404; not needed for status

feature_results.rationale: Copilot CLI programmatic mode (-p, --no-ask-user, --allow-* flags, --output-format json JSONL, -s) is documented for scripts and CI/CD, including a GitHub Actions guide with token-based auth. Documented exit codes (0/1/2/130) are given for `copilot workflow run`; exit-code semantics for plain `-p` runs were not found in the pages read.

evidence.excerpt: This allows you to use Copilot programmatically in scripts, CI/CD pipelines, and automation workflows.
Set the output format: `text` (the default) or `json`. With `json`, the CLI emits JSONL (one JSON object per line)
Prevent the agent from pausing to seek additional user input.
The workflow completed successfully and any requested result file was written successfully.
You can run GitHub Copilot CLI in a GitHub Actions workflow to automate AI-powered tasks as part of your CI/CD process.

constraints.description: Unattended tool use requires explicit approval flags (e.g. --allow-tool, --allow-all-tools); exit codes are documented specifically for `copilot workflow run`.
Requires a Copilot license and a token (fine-grained PAT with Copilot Requests permission, etc.).

feature_results.rationale: Official docs describe ghost-text suggestions offered automatically while typing, accepted with Tab, across multiple IDEs; the feature matrix shows code completion supported in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode and Neovim. Also includes next edit suggestions.

evidence.excerpt: GitHub Copilot offers coding suggestions as you type. For example, in a Java file, create a class by typing `class Test`.
GitHub Copilot will automatically suggest a class body in grayed text. To accept the suggestion, press Tab.
Although inline suggestion functionality is available across all these extensions, chat functionality is currently available only in Visual Studio Code, JetBrains, and Visual Studio.

constraints.description: Available as an extension in Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, Vim, Neovim, JetBrains IDEs, and Azure Data Studio (product page); feature matrix also lists Eclipse and Xcode.
Copilot Free offers limited functionality; users need Free or a paid plan.

feature_results.rationale: Official FAQ documents both an optional duplication detection filter (public-code match blocking, admin-enforceable at enterprise/org level) and IP indemnification for unmodified suggestions when filtering is enabled, tied to organizational plans.

evidence.excerpt: This filter can be enabled by the administrator for your enterprise and it can apply for all organizations within your enterprise, or the administrator can defer control to individual organizations.
You’re entitled to IP indemnification from GitHub for the unmodified suggestions when Copilot’s filtering is enabled.
The primary differences between the organization offerings and the individual offering are license management, policy management, and IP indemnity.

constraints.description: IP indemnity is an organization-plan (Business/Enterprise) benefit; individual plans exclude it. Indemnity requires the duplication filter to be enabled and covers unmodified suggestions.

feature_results.rationale: Personal, repository (path-specific, repo-wide, agent) and organization instructions are supported, with a documented precedence order for Copilot Chat on GitHub.com. Other clients combine files without a defined general order.

evidence.excerpt: For Copilot Chat on GitHub.com, all relevant instructions are provided to Copilot. The order of precedence, from highest to lowest, is:
Personal instructions; Repository custom instructions (Path-specific, Repository-wide, Agent instructions); Organization custom instructions

constraints.description: Documented precedence applies to Copilot Chat on GitHub.com; most other surfaces, including CLI, VS Code and Visual Studio, combine instruction files without a general precedence order. Organization instructions only supported in Chat on GitHub.com, code review on GitHub.com and cloud agent on GitHub.com.
Organization custom instructions require Copilot Business or Enterprise.

feature_results.rationale: Official docs describe configuring Copilot CLI to use a customer-controlled model endpoint, explicitly including locally running models such as Ollama, vLLM and Foundry Local, via environment variables. No separate Copilot license is needed in local BYOK setups per the GHES docs.

evidence.excerpt: This lets you connect to OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Azure OpenAI, or Anthropic, including locally running models such as Ollama.
A Copilot license is required for all Copilot functionality, with the exception of local "bring your own key" (BYOK) setups.

constraints.description: Documented for Copilot CLI; models must support tool calling and streaming (128k+ context recommended). Other surfaces (e.g. IDE BYOK) were not confirmed in this pass.

queries: fetch docs.github.com Copilot CLI BYOK models page
fetch docs.github.com Copilot BYOK in VS Code (404)

feature_results.rationale: Documented mechanisms: semantic repository indexing, automatic context compaction in long sessions, large tool-output offloading, subagents with separate context, and full-repository context gathering in code review.

evidence.excerpt: For the Copilot CLI, when your conversation reaches approximately 80% of the context window's capacity, Copilot CLI automatically starts compacting the context in the background.
Indexing runs in the background and initial indexing can take up to 60 seconds for a large repository.
This capability analyzes your entire repository to better understand the context of code changes.

constraints.description: Compaction is available in most clients but not Xcode; controls vary by client and surface.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub documents MCP support across IDEs, Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and cloud agent, plus a CLI plugin system and a GitHub MCP Registry for third-party servers.

evidence.excerpt: You can use MCP to extend the capabilities of GitHub Copilot by integrating it with a wide range of existing tools and services.
MCP servers are supported in Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Xcode, and Eclipse.
GitHub Copilot CLI supports both local and remote MCP servers.

constraints.description: Business/Enterprise organizations must enable the 'MCP servers in Copilot' policy, which is disabled by default.

queries: fetch: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Copilot docs
fetch: Copilot CLI command reference (copilot mcp / copilot plugin)

feature_results.rationale: GitHub Mobile (iOS/Android official app) provides Copilot Chat; docs describe asking Copilot questions in it.

evidence.excerpt: GitHub Mobile | Chatting with Copilot while away from your main development environment.
Ask coding questions, explore repositories, and get help with pull requests in GitHub Mobile.

constraints.description: Organization/enterprise policies may restrict access to Copilot Chat in GitHub Mobile.

queries: fetch: Where to use GitHub Copilot
fetch: Asking GitHub Copilot questions in GitHub Mobile

feature_results.rationale: Copilot CLI documents delegation to built-in and custom subagents with separate contexts, plus /fleet (and --fleet) to run subagents in parallel, monitored via /tasks.

evidence.excerpt: When you use this command, Copilot assigns separate parts of the work to subagents.
A subagent is **an agent doing delegated work** in a separate context window.

constraints.description: /fleet and --fleet are Copilot CLI features; --fleet is not supported in ACP server mode.

feature_results.rationale: Agent mode takes one high-level prompt and decides which files to change, editing files across the project; the cloud agent also returns changes as pull requests.

evidence.excerpt: Give Copilot a task and let it work autonomously in your editor, editing files across your project and running commands until the task is complete.
Copilot determines which files to make changes to, offers code changes and terminal commands to complete the task, and iterates to remediate issues until the original task is complete.

constraints.description: Agent mode available in VS Code, Visual Studio (17.14+), JetBrains, Xcode, Eclipse; may be disabled by administrators.

feature_results.rationale: Officially supported in Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Eclipse and Xcode.

evidence.excerpt: Your IDE (Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Eclipse, and XCode)

constraints.description: Feature availability varies per IDE; GitHub points to a Copilot feature matrix for comparison.

queries: fetch: Where to use GitHub Copilot

feature_results.rationale: Docs state images and PDFs can be attached to chat prompts, with explicit examples of generating code from a UI mockup or generating HTML from a web page screenshot. Availability depends on the selected model supporting image input; the feature matrix marks Vision as preview in VS Code/JetBrains/Xcode.

evidence.excerpt: You can attach images and PDFs to your prompts when using a model that supports image input.
A mockup of the user interface for an application and ask Copilot to generate the code.
A screenshot of a web page and ask Copilot to generate HTML for a similar page.

constraints.description: Requires a model that supports image input.
Feature matrix lists Vision as preview (P) in VS Code, JetBrains, Xcode; supported (✓) in Visual Studio and Eclipse; not supported in Neovim.
Image and PDF attachments are available on all Copilot plans and enabled by default.

feature_results.rationale: Docs state Copilot can build applications from natural-language descriptions and write code from natural-language prompts, from comment-driven suggestions up to multi-file agent output.

evidence.excerpt: **Build applications** from natural-language descriptions.
**Write code** with inline suggestions and natural-language prompts.
You can also describe something you want to do using natural language within a comment, and Copilot will suggest the code to accomplish your goal.

constraints.description: Capabilities depend on Copilot plan, client, and organization policies; Free tier is limited.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot is cloud-hosted (GitHub.com and GHE.com) and not available as a self-hosted product. The only on-prem-adjacent option is a technical-preview air-gapped Copilot CLI setup with GitHub Enterprise Server and an administrator-configured model provider; this is narrow and not full feature parity. GHE.com is a dedicated-region cloud offering, not customer infrastructure.

evidence.excerpt: Alternatively, you can configure Copilot CLI to work with GitHub Enterprise Server in disconnected or air-gapped environments, without connecting to GitHub's cloud platforms or requiring a Copilot license.
This feature is in technical preview and subject to change.
Copilot is not currently available for GitHub Enterprise Server.

constraints.description: Air-gapped Copilot CLI with GHES is in technical preview.
Requires GitHub Enterprise Server and an administrator-configured model provider; Copilot Chat and other features are not integrated into GHES.

queries: fetch About GitHub Copilot on GitHub Enterprise Server

feature_results.rationale: Docs describe running several Copilot CLI sessions side by side with a sessions sidebar, and multiple cloud agent sessions tracked from the agents panel; cloud sandboxes are also described as enabling multiple tasks in parallel.

evidence.excerpt: You're not limited to one session at a time. You can keep several running side by side and switch between them.
run multiple tasks in parallel
Use the agents panel on GitHub to monitor and manage agent sessions across your repositories.

constraints.description: Cloud sandboxes are in public preview.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot CLI offers per-tool-category allow/deny (shell, write, read, MCP tools, URLs, with subcommand patterns), session vs persisted approvals, and broader allow-all/autopilot options; read-only operations are auto-allowed while modifying ones prompt.

evidence.excerpt: The `--allow-tool` and `--deny-tool` options allow or deny permission for specific tools, or tool subcommands.
Deny rules always take precedence over allow rules, even when `--allow-all` is set or a matching approval has been saved in `permissions-config.json`.

constraints.description: On Copilot Business/Enterprise, allow-all options may be blocked by an enterprise administrator.
Documented here for Copilot CLI; other surfaces were not assessed.

feature_results.rationale: Repository instruction files (.github/copilot-instructions.md, path-specific .instructions.md, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md) persist and apply automatically; Copilot Memory additionally stores repo facts and user preferences across sessions.

evidence.excerpt: Instead of repeatedly adding the same context to your prompts, you can create custom instructions that automatically provide this information to Copilot to allow it to generate higher quality responses.
These are specified in a `copilot-instructions.md` file in the `.github` directory of the repository.
Copilot Memory helps Copilot become more effective over time by remembering facts about your repositories and your personal coding preferences.

constraints.description: Copilot Memory is in public preview; used by cloud agent, code review, CLI and agentic autofix.
Support for instruction file types varies by client and surface.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot CLI plan mode (Shift+Tab) produces an implementation plan with the user before any code is written; on completion the user chooses to accept the plan and continue in Autopilot (optionally with /fleet) or exit plan mode.

evidence.excerpt: Plan mode lets you collaborate with Copilot on an implementation plan before any code is written.
**Accept plan and continue in Autopilot execution mode + /fleet** to allow Copilot to use subagents and work autonomously to implement the plan without any further input.

constraints.description: Documented for Copilot CLI interactive sessions; other surfaces were not assessed.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot CLI can create PRs on GitHub.com on the user's behalf; the cloud agent also opens PRs.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot creates a pull request on GitHub.com, on your behalf. You are marked as the pull request author.
Push the new branch and create a pull request.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot offers local sandboxing (OS-level restriction of commands, enabled with /sandbox enable, off by default, lighter-weight than a VM) and cloud sandboxing (entire session in an isolated ephemeral GitHub-hosted Linux environment, public preview, usage-billed). Cloud agent also runs in an ephemeral cloud environment.

evidence.excerpt: Cloud sandboxing: Run an entire Copilot session remotely, inside a fully isolated, ephemeral Linux environment hosted by GitHub.
Local sandboxing is turned off by default.
To enable it, run /sandbox enable inside a session.

constraints.description: Cloud sandboxes are in public preview.
Available in Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app; local sandboxing on macOS, Linux and recent Windows 11 builds; it does not run commands in a separate VM or container. Off by default.
Cloud sandboxing is billed based on usage; local sandboxing at no extra charge.

feature_results.rationale: Copilot automations natively run cloud agent tasks on an hourly/daily/weekly schedule without a user session. Copilot CLI also has experimental /every and /after commands, though these fire only while a session is open.

constraints.description: Automations available on Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise; Business/Enterprise need admin to enable cloud agent.
